challenge.better_approach: Considered raising ticket-refused-<id>-at-<gate> (the identity failed() uses). But the clearance gate's take carries no passed field, so nothing would ever clear that refusal at clearance. Keeping the identity and fixing the why is the smallest true record.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a holder's refusal always carries a reason. The clearance gate's every accepted False path sets reason (codemother clearance/gate.py queueme). A reasonless refusal falls back to the old wording.
challenge.prior_art: 41a5bae3d01b built the clear-on-take for this identity; 0bcb816d6e9c separated silence from a refusal for chart and verdict gates, by reading the ticket's own record. Neither touched the why text for a direct refusal.
challenge.real_collision: none: 41a5bae3d01b's identity and clearing are kept, and 794835a34ec9's refused identity is untouched.

answers.falsifier: A refused reply raises a why that names the refusal and the reason, not 'no handler took it'. A bounce and a timeout still say no handler. A later take clears the trouble.
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: 9 live troubles ticket-unqueued-*-at-clearance in ~/.cairn/logs/cairn/0/troubletickets/ (bin/cairn trouble live --json, 2026-11-16), every occurrence's reply a refusal with a reason
answers.how: In cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py Ticket.queueme, a reply with accepted False, no is_bounce, no error, and a reason is worded as '<holder> refused it: <first line of reason>'. A bounce or a timeout keeps 'no handler took it'. The identity ticket-unqueued-<id>-at-<gate> is unchanged, so 41a5bae3d01b's clear-on-take still works. A red-first proof scripts the three replies into a scratch ticket.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth never collapses an error into a coherent shape. Every one of the 12 occurrences said no handler took the ask, when the gate took it and refused.
answers.what: When a gate answers a ticket's queueme and refuses, the trouble the ticket raises says the holder refused and carries its reason, instead of saying no handler took it.

bullets.text: All 9 clearance 'unqueued' troubles were the gate refusing with a reason, recorded as 'no handler took it'. The trouble now says the gate refused and why.

title: When a gate answers a ticket's queueme and refuses, the trouble the ticket raises says the holder refused and carries it
